questions.question: Explain the difference between 0/1 knapsack and unbounded knapsack in Dynamic Programming.
questions.ideal_answer: 0/1 knapsack and unbounded knapsack differ in several ways: 0/1 knapsack is item inclusion binary choice (works by each item at most once) whereas unbounded knapsack is unlimited item copies (works by complete knapsack). 0/1 knapsack is typically used for dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], val[i] + dp[i-1][w-wt[i]]), while unbounded knapsack is used for dp[w] = max over all items of (val[i] + dp[w-wt[i]]). Example demonstrating 0/1 knapsack: for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) for (int w = W; w >= wt[i]; w--) dp[w] = Math.max(dp[w], dp[w-wt[i]] + val[i]);. Example demonstrating unbounded knapsack: for (int w = 0; w <= W; w++) for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (wt[i] <= w) dp[w] = Math.max(dp[w], dp[w-wt[i]] + val[i]);.
